description_full: HELPING WITHOUT TAKING OVER﻿: MOTIVATION, BOUNDARIES, FAMILY CONFLICT, SCREENS & GROWING INDEPENDENCE Wednesday, November 18, 2026 6:30–8:00 p.m. Virtual Event You remind them to get up. You manage the deadlines. You check whether things are getting done. And when they aren't, you step in -- because you're afraid of what will happen if you don't. Somewhere along the way, you've become responsible for keeping everything moving. For parents of neurodivergent teens and young adults, it's an exhausting place to be. But stepping back completely isn't always the answer, either. So how do you help without taking over? Dr. Rick Silver and an expert panel will explore how to: Stop the cycle of reminding, rescuing, and arguing Understand why your young person may be struggling Set realistic expectations without constant conflict Gradually transfer responsibility while maintaining support The goal isn't to do less for your child, it's to help in ways that build their ability to do more. Visit registration page. Sponsored by Thrive Emerge. Free

description_full: UNDERSTANDING MARYLAND ABLE ACCOUNTS Wednesday, November 18, 2026 7:00-8:00 p.m. Virtual Event Maryland ABLE accounts are a way to help individuals with disabilities save money and pay for qualified disability-related expenses (including living expenses, education, housing, transportation, assistive technology, and much more) without jeopardizing state or federal means-tested benefits such as SSI or Medicaid. Come hear about how it works, the benefits and eligibility. Visit registration page. rsforautism.org/calendar/?calendertype=month&type=&eventname=&yearvar=2026&month=11 Sponsored by Pathfinders for Autism and Maryland ABLE. Free

description_full: PARENT’S GUIDE TO CHALLENGING BEHAVIORS Thursday, November 19, 2026 1:00 p.m. Virtual Event Discover a proven, research-based approach to better understand your child’s behavior and what influences it. Learn practical tools to prevent challenging behaviors—and handle them calmly when they do occur. Ask questions, gain ready-to-use strategies and leave feeling more confident in your parenting. For parents of children ages 2–8. Visit registration page. Although this event is not specifically for families of children with a developmental delay or disability, the information may be useful.
